newsitem.title: USA: Death penalty upheld for Fla. anti-abortion killer.
newsitem.headline: Death penalty upheld for Fla. anti-abortion killer.

text.p: The Florida Supreme Court Wednesday upheld the conviction of Paul Hill, a former minister who was sentenced to die for the 1994 murder of a doctor and his assistant outside a Pensacola abortion clinic.

In a unanimous ruling, the court rejected arguments from Hill's attorneys, who were assigned to the case over the objections of their client. Hill was convicted of gunning down Dr. John Britton and James Barrett outside the Ladies Centre in Pensacola.

His lawyers argued that the lower court erred in allowing Hill to represent himself and in barring him from using justifiable homicide as a defence. They also claimed the death penalty was too severe a punishment, partly because Hill thought he was morally justified in the double murder.
The court rejected all the defence arguments. It held that, as a practical matter, permitting a defendant to justify criminal activity in such a manner "would be an invitation for lawlessness."

Hill faces death in Florida's electric chair. During his trial, he presented no evidence in his defence but argued that his killings were justified because Britton performed abortions at the clinic, a long-standing target of anti-abortion groups.
Hill's attorney could not be reached immediately for comment on the state supreme court's ruling.
